method: Exact biquadratic root extraction for complex wavenumbers in thermoelasticity, low/high-frequency and small-coupling asymptotic series with explicit validity intervals, and perturbation analysis of magnetothermoelastic specific loss
main_result: Derives exact real/imaginary wavenumber formulas for classical thermoelastic plane waves, corrects Chadwick-Sneddon's specific-loss extremum frequency from (1 +- epsilon)^(1/2) to the exact critical frequency Omega = 1 + epsilon for both E- and T-modes, and shows transverse magnetic fields shift specific-loss extrema to higher frequencies
validation: Numerical verification of asymptotic expansions (valid for Omega < (1+epsilon)^2/2 and Omega > 6) against exact complex roots
stated_limitations: Uses classical parabolic Fourier heat conduction (infinite high-frequency thermal speed) and small thermomechanical/magnetoelastic coupling perturbations for the MTE case
future_work: None explicitly stated

title: Fractional Thermoelasticity
journal: Solid Mechanics and Its Applications, Vol. 219, Springer (Monograph)
model_constitutive: Quasi-static uncoupled fractional thermoelasticity (and diffusive stresses) driven by Caputo time-fractional (0 < alpha <= 2), Riesz space-fractional, and space-time-fractional Fourier and Cattaneo/telegraph heat/diffusion equations with power-law and Mittag-Leffler kernels
geometry: 1D slabs/half-spaces, 2D/3D infinite media, polar/cylindrical/spherical cavities and solid cylinders/spheres, Kirchhoff-Love thin shells, and advection-diffusion planes
method: Laplace, Fourier, sin/cos, Hankel, Weber, and Legendre integral transforms yielding closed-form Mittag-Leffler, Wright, Mainardi, and Bessel integral representations under physical vs mathematical Neumann/Robin BCs
main_result: Establishes a systematic analytical handbook of fundamental temperature and thermal/diffusive stress solutions across Cartesian, cylindrical, spherical, and thin-shell geometries, showing continuous interpolation between localized diffusion (alpha=0), classical thermoelasticity (alpha=1), and wave-without-dissipation thermoelasticity (alpha=2)
validation: Analytical limiting-case checks at alpha = 0, 1, 2 against classical Carslaw-Jaeger/Nowacki thermoelasticity and Green-Naghdi Type II wave fronts plus numerical stress profiles
stated_limitations: Predominantly quasi-static uncoupled thermoelasticity (neglecting inertia u_tt and dilatational thermomechanical coupling in the heat equation) to keep Laplace-Hankel inversions analytically tractable; no experimental parameter fitting
future_work: Extend fractional constitutive models to fully coupled dynamical inertia-thermoelasticity, nonperfect contact interfaces, and experimental identification of fractional orders

title: Fractional Cattaneo-Type Equations and Generalized Thermoelasticity
model_constitutive: Time-fractional Cattaneo-type heat conduction (replacing first/second time derivatives in Cattaneo's law by Caputo fractional derivatives of orders alpha, beta in (0, 2]) coupled to quasi-static isotropic thermal stresses
geometry: Infinite 1D medium and axisymmetric 2D plane under Dirac delta initial/source thermal pulses
method: Laplace and Fourier/Hankel integral transforms with Mittag-Leffler function representations and numerical integral evaluation
main_result: Formulates generalized fractional Cattaneo thermoelasticity interpolating between telegrapher/Lord-Shulman heat waves (alpha=1) and undamped wave equations (alpha->2), computing fundamental temperature and stress profiles in 1D and 2D axisymmetric geometries
validation: Exact analytical reduction to classical diffusion (tau=0, alpha=1), standard Cattaneo telegrapher jump/singularity fronts (alpha=1), and wave equation fronts (alpha=2)
stated_limitations: Uncoupled quasi-static stress calculation (neglects mechanical inertia and dilatation heating); numerical resolution leaves open whether wavefront jump vs continuous rapid transition occurs as alpha -> 1
future_work: Rigorously resolve wavefront continuity vs discontinuity behavior of the fractional telegrapher solution near alpha -> 1 and include full dynamical coupling

title: A Nonlinear Theory of Elastic Materials with Voids
authors: Jace W. Nunziato; Stephen C. Cowin
journal: Archive for Rational Mechanics and Analysis
model_constitutive: Finite-deformation nonlinear and linearized theory of elastic porous solids with independent matrix volume-fraction scalar field nu(X, t), equilibrated inertia k*nu_tt, equilibrated stress vector h ~ grad(nu), and internal equilibrated body force g (viscoelastic void-rate damping)
geometry: Arbitrary 3D finite-strain porous body; homogeneous void compression/compaction states; 1D plane harmonic waves in linear isotropic void-elastic media
method: Goodman-Cowin equilibrated force/energy balance, Coleman-Noll thermodynamic restrictions, isotropic tensor invariant representation, and linearized dispersion/stability analysis
main_result: Constructs the foundational nonlinear and linear Cowin-Nunziato theory of elastic materials with voids, derives thermodynamic concavity/dissipation inequalities, characterizes pure void compaction vs matrix compression regimes, and shows linear isotropic media support an uncoupled shear wave plus two coupled dispersive/attenuated dilatational-porosity modes above a void resonance cutoff frequency
validation: Thermodynamic consistency proofs, reduction to classical elasticity as void volume fraction vanishes or locks, and qualitative agreement with porous rock/ceramic compaction curves
stated_limitations: Purely mechanical isothermal formulation in the main wave/homogeneous-deformation sections (voids contain no pore fluid pressure); phenomenological equilibrated inertia coefficient k lacks direct micromechanical measurement
future_work: Calibrate void moduli and equilibrated inertia from ultrasonic dispersion/compaction experiments on porous rocks, soils, ceramics, and pressed powders

title: Thermoelastic Waves in Solids with Thermal Relaxation
model_constitutive: Linear isotropic Lord-Shulman generalized thermoelasticity with Maxwell-Cattaneo thermal relaxation time tau
geometry: Unbounded 3D isotropic thermoelastic medium (plane harmonic waves) and traction-free thermally insulated/conducting isotropic half-space (Rayleigh surface waves)
method: Exact dispersion analysis supplemented by matched inner/outer singular perturbation expansions in small thermomechanical coupling epsilon around the resonant crossover tau*omega ~ 1 / wave-speed coincidence point
main_result: Derives explicit small-coupling outer expansions AND singular inner expansions (near the thermal-elastic speed coincidence point 1/tau ~ 0.2817 where naive perturbation breaks down) for bulk plane waves and thermoelastic Rayleigh surface waves
validation: Matched asymptotic inner/outer curves verified quantitatively against exact numerical roots of the Lord-Shulman Rayleigh secular equation and reduced to Lockett/Chadwick classical limits as tau -> 0
stated_limitations: Isotropic homogeneous linear solid with small thermomechanical coupling epsilon << 1 in asymptotic formulas
future_work: None explicitly stated

title: Experimental Evidence of Hyperbolic Heat Conduction in Processed Meat
authors: K. Mitra; S. Kumar; A. Vedavarz; M. K. Moallemi
journal: Journal of Heat Transfer (Transactions of the ASME)
model_constitutive: 1D macroscopic Cattaneo-Vernotte hyperbolic heat conduction equation tau*(d^2T/dt^2) + dT/dt = alpha*(d^2T/dx^2) with relaxation time tau ~ 15.5 +- 2.1 s
geometry: Contacting cold/warm slabs (Experiments I-III) and sudden boundary cooling/heating of cylindrical processed bologna and raw pork samples (Experiments IV-V)
method: Embedded micro-thermocouple transient temperature recordings compared against exact analytical superposition solutions of the 1D hyperbolic telegrapher equation vs parabolic Fourier diffusion
main_result: Reports sharp finite-speed step-like thermal wavefront jumps and delayed temperature response in processed bologna meat fitted by a macroscopic thermal relaxation time tau ~ 15.5 s, deviating strongly from classical Fourier predictions
validation: Four independent contact configuration tests (cold-warm, cold-medium-warm, symmetric three-layer, aluminium-plate boundary) plus preliminary raw pork test
stated_limitations: Thermocouple response-time (~20-40 ms), imperfect contact resistance, and moisture/phase effects in heterogeneous biological tissue (note: later critically re-evaluated in literature such as Herwig-Beckert and Azhdari et al. 2026 in this corpus)
future_work: Extend experimental measurements to raw pork and diverse biological tissues to quantify macroscopic non-Fourier effects in bio-heat applications

title: On First Strain-Gradient Theories in Linear Elasticity
authors: R. D. Mindlin; N. N. Eshel
journal: International Journal of Solids and Structures
model_constitutive: Isotropic and anisotropic linear first strain-gradient elasticity in three equivalent potential-energy forms: Form I (second gradient of displacement u_k,ij), Form II (first gradient of strain epsilon_ij,k), and Form III (rotation gradient kappa_ij + symmetric dilatational/deviatoric strain gradients)
geometry: Arbitrary 3D piecewise-smooth bounded elastic body V with smooth surface S and sharp edges C
method: Surface-gradient divergence-theorem reductions establishing exact stress/double-stress/traction/edge-force conversion formulas across Forms I-III, plus first-principles linear/angular momentum and energy balance derivation
main_result: Proves complete mathematical equivalence of the field equations, traction/double-traction boundary conditions, edge forces, and uniqueness theorems across all three forms of first strain-gradient elasticity (5 isotropic gradient constants + 2 Lame constants), and resolves couple-stress / angular-momentum ambiguities by identifying true tangential couple traction
validation: Exact tensorial identity proofs across Forms I, II, and III and reduction to Toupin-Mindlin couple-stress theory when symmetric strain-gradient moduli vanish
stated_limitations: Static/linear isothermal elasticity; uniqueness requires sufficient boundary/corner regularity and supplementary limit conditions near concentrated loads/singularities to avoid Sternberg-Muki pseudo-solutions
future_work: None explicitly stated

title: Second Gradient of Strain and Surface-Tension in Linear Elasticity
journal: International Journal of Solids and Structures
model_constitutive: Linear isotropic second-strain-gradient elasticity with potential energy W(epsilon_ij, epsilon_ij,k, epsilon_ij,kl) containing 16 higher-order isotropic constants plus 2 initial-gradient cohesion moduli b_0, yielding 6th-order equilibrium PDEs
geometry: Arbitrary 3D body with smooth boundary, separated planar half-space (cleavage surface tension), solid elastic sphere of radius r_0, and infinite medium with spherical cavity of radius r_0
method: Divergence-theorem derivation of 6th-order field equations and triple-stress boundary conditions, Papkovich-Boussinesq Helmholtz-factorized stress-function representation, and exact planar/spherical boundary-layer solutions
main_result: Demonstrates that including second gradients of strain makes cohesive force and free-surface tension intrinsic to continuum elasticity, matches Gazis-Wallis lattice cleavage strain profiles, and derives curvature-dependent surface tension T = T_0 / (1 + (8*b_1/b_0)*l_1*kappa) (Tolman-like size correction) for spheres and cavities
validation: Comparison with discrete 1D multi-neighbor crystal lattice surface-relaxation model and reduction to classical Young-Laplace sphere dilatation as l_i/r_0 -> 0
stated_limitations: Static linear isothermal elasticity; contains 16+2 material constants that are difficult to measure macroscopically without atomistic/lattice input
future_work: None explicitly stated

title: Method of Lagrange Multipliers for Exploitation of the Entropy Principle
journal: Archive for Rational Mechanics and Analysis
model_constitutive: General continuum/extended thermodynamics with Muller's supply-free entropy inequality (decoupling entropy flux Phi_i from q_i/T) applied specifically to thermoelastic fluids/solids with Cattaneo-like thermal relaxation
geometry: Arbitrary 3D continuum subject to first-order quasi-linear balance PDEs
method: Algebraic lemma proving equivalence between constrained linear inequalities and unconstrained Lagrange-multiplier inequalities, justified via Cauchy-Kowalewski local analytic initial-value solvability
main_result: Establishes Liu's Lagrange-multiplier theorem converting constrained Muller entropy exploitation into unconstrained algebraic identities, and illustrates it on Cattaneo-type heat-conducting elastic fluids where coldness Lambda^epsilon differs from 1/T at O(tau^2)
validation: Rigorous algebraic proof of Liu's Lemma and Cauchy-Kowalewski admissibility proof for analytic balance systems
stated_limitations: Rigorous realization of arbitrary initial spatial derivatives requires real-analytic constitutive functions and non-characteristic Cauchy hypersurfaces (Cauchy-Kowalewski hypotheses)
future_work: Broad application across extended thermodynamic and non-classical continuum constitutive theories

title: Moore-Gibson-Thompson equation with memory, part II: General decay of energy
model_constitutive: Subcritical linear Moore-Gibson-Thompson (MGT) equation with general convex memory kernel g(s) satisfying g'(t) <= -H(g(t)): tau*u_ttt + alpha*u_tt + c^2*A*u + b*A*u_t - int_0^t g(t-s)*A*w(s) ds = 0 (Types I, II, III: w = u, u_t, u + tau*u_t)
geometry: Bounded smooth domain Omega subset R^n (abstract strictly positive selfadjoint operator A)
method: Nonlinear convex ODE comparison principle (Lasiecka-Tataru / Alabau-Boussouira method), Jensen's inequality on history integrals, and Lyapunov multiplier energy estimates
main_result: Proves that in the subcritical regime gamma = alpha - tau*c^2/b > 0, the total MGT-memory energy decays at a rate governed directly by the ODE s_t + c*H(s) = 0 of the relaxation kernel g (recovering exponential, polynomial, or logarithmic decay as special cases)
validation: Rigorous PDE energy-decay proofs recovering Part I exponential-kernel theorems when H(s) is linear and matching viscoelastic optimal decay rates
stated_limitations: Restricted to the subcritical MGT regime gamma > 0 and convex positive-decreasing kernels g with smallness/positivity conditions
future_work: Critical-case gamma = 0 behavior with general memory kernels (addressed subsequently by Dell'Oro, Lasiecka & Pata 2016)

title: On Waves in an Elastic Plate
journal: Proceedings of the Royal Society of London. Series A
model_constitutive: Classical 2D plane-strain linear isotropic elastodynamics (Lame constants lambda, mu, density rho)
geometry: Infinite homogeneous isotropic elastic plate of finite thickness 2f bounded by parallel traction-free planes y = +-f
method: Compressional/shear potential decomposition separated into symmetric (extensional) and antisymmetric (flexural) modes yielding the Rayleigh-Lamb hyperbolic/trigonometric transcendental period equations
main_result: Derives and numerically solves the symmetric and antisymmetric Rayleigh-Lamb dispersion equations across wavelengths, connecting long-wave thin-plate extensional/flexural limits to short-wave Rayleigh surface-wave asymptotes, Lame modes (xi*f = s*pi/sqrt(2)), and thickness-stretch/shear cut-off frequencies
validation: Analytical long-wave (Rayleigh/Kirchhoff plate), short-wave (Rayleigh surface wave), and exact thickness-resonance checks plus numerical tables/dispersion curves for Poisson's solid (lambda = mu)
stated_limitations: Homogeneous, isotropic, traction-free, isothermal single plate in vacuum; notes phase velocity V -> inf near cut-offs is purely kinematical whereas signal speed of local disturbances remains bounded
future_work: Motivates extension toward seismic waves in an elastic stratum resting on a dissimilar half-space

title: Extended Irreversible Thermodynamics (Fourth Edition)
authors: David Jou; Jose Casas-Vazquez; Georgy Lebon
model_constitutive: Extended Irreversible Thermodynamics (EIT) elevating dissipative fluxes (heat flux q, viscous pressure tensor P^v, higher-order flux hierarchies Q^(n)) to independent state variables in generalized non-equilibrium entropy s(u, v, q, P^v, ...), covering Cattaneo, Guyer-Krumhansl, ballistic-diffusion, continued-fraction k/omega transport, viscoelastic rheology, micro/nanoscale phonon radiative transfer, semiconductors, and cosmology
geometry: Bulk continua, dielectric crystals, thin silicon/graphene nanofilms and nanowires, non-Fickian polymer slabs, Poiseuille channels, shock waves, and cosmological horizons
method: Generalized Gibbs equation, Second Law positivity of entropy production, kinetic/Boltzmann/information-theory/fluctuation-dissipation closures, continued-fraction asymptotic resummation of infinite flux hierarchies, and boundary-slip modeling
main_result: Provides a comprehensive physical and mathematical framework unifying hyperbolic transport, Guyer-Krumhansl nonlocal heat flow, and nanoscale size-dependent effective thermal conductivity kappa_eff(L/l) (via continued-fraction flux hierarchies and phonon hydrodynamics) with non-equilibrium temperature/entropy definitions
validation: Quantitative comparisons against light/neutron scattering, high-frequency ultrasound, silicon thin-film/nanowire thermal conductivity vs Knudsen number, polymer sorption, and cryogenic/semiconductor transport data
stated_limitations: Phenomenological relaxation times and correlation lengths require kinetic-theory or MD calibration; boundary conditions for higher-order tensorial fluxes at walls/interfaces remain delicate at large Knudsen numbers
future_work: Further clarify nonequilibrium temperature/boundary conditions in nanosystems, nonlinear far-from-equilibrium fluctuations, biological/active matter transport, and coupled thermomechanical nanosystems

title: Second Sound in NaF
authors: Howard E. Jackson; Charles T. Walker; Thomas F. McNelly
model_constitutive: Cryogenic phonon hydrodynamics: ballistic longitudinal/transverse phonon pulses transitioning via normal (N) vs resistive/umklapp (R) phonon scattering into collective second-sound waves
geometry: Ultra-pure multi-grown NaF single crystal (~2-5x fewer impurities than McNelly et al., peak thermal conductivity 240 W/(cm*K) at 16.5 K) under transient heat-pulse propagation
method: Time-of-flight heat-pulse arrival-time measurements from 8 K to 20 K combined with Callaway thermal-conductivity scattering-rate analysis
main_result: Demonstrates clean separation of longitudinal ballistic, transverse ballistic, and collective second-sound pulses in ultra-pure NaF between ~10 K and 19 K, and discovers that at the highest temperatures the second-sound pulse arrival time continues increasing rather than leveling off at the theoretical Debye hydrodynamic value v_II
validation: Direct experimental pulse arrival-time traces across 8-20 K benchmarked against lower-purity NaF (McNelly et al. 1970) and solid He data
stated_limitations: Cryogenic regime only (10-19 K); anomalous departure from constant theoretical v_II at T > 15 K is unexplained by isotropic dispersionless Debye second-sound theory
future_work: Publish full Callaway scattering-rate decomposition and account theoretically for phonon dispersion/umklapp effects on high-T second-sound speed

title: Energy-Flux Vector of Surface Thermoelastic Waves
model_constitutive: Classical linear coupled isotropic thermoelasticity (Fourier heat conduction)
geometry: Homogeneous isotropic traction-free half-space z >= 0 with convective/radiation thermal boundary condition dT/dz + h*T = 0
method: Time-averaged thermomechanical energy-flux vector computation (mechanical Poynting-like work rate + conductive heat flux) for complex-wavenumber thermoelastic Rayleigh E-mode and T-mode
main_result: Proves that unlike purely elastic Rayleigh waves whose mean energy flux is strictly parallel to the free surface, the mean energy-flux vector of thermoelastic surface waves tilts relative to the surface at an angle varying strongly with depth z and dimensionless frequency while decaying exponentially in both depth and propagation direction
validation: Analytical reduction to parallel elastic Rayleigh flux as thermomechanical coupling vanishes plus numerical depth/frequency angle profiles for aluminium/metal parameters
stated_limitations: Classical parabolic Fourier heat conduction only; linear isotropic homogeneous half-space
future_work: None explicitly stated

title: Generalization of Selective Integration Procedures to Anisotropic and Nonlinear Media
journal: International Journal for Numerical Methods in Engineering
model_constitutive: Computational solid mechanics: B-bar (assumed dilatational strain-displacement matrix) finite element formulation for nearly-incompressible general anisotropic and finite-strain nonlinear continua
geometry: Arbitrary 2D/3D continuum discretized by isoparametric bilinear/trilinear finite elements
method: Projection replacement of the volumetric part of the discrete strain-displacement operator B_dil by an element-averaged/reduced-quadrature B_bar_dil while retaining full quadrature on deviatoric terms
main_result: Introduces the B-bar method, removing volumetric locking in nearly incompressible elements while remaining valid for arbitrary anisotropic elasticity and large-deformation elastoplasticity where classical selective reduced integration fails to decouple volumetric and deviatoric energy
validation: Exact algebraic specialization proofs showing B-bar reduces to selective integration (isotropic linear) and Nagtegaal-Parks-Rice mean-dilatation quadrilaterals
stated_limitations: Purely numerical/discretization methodology note; does not present new continuum physics or large-scale numerical benchmarks in this short communication
future_work: Apply B-bar elements broadly across nonlinear anisotropic elastoplastic and incompressible structural codes

title: Observation of second sound in graphite at temperatures above 100 K
authors: S. Huberman; R. A. Duncan; K. Chen; B. Song; V. Chiloyan; Z. Ding; A. A. Maznev; G. Chen; K. A. Nelson
model_constitutive: Ab initio linearized phonon Boltzmann Transport Equation (BTE) with exact three-phonon normal/umklapp collision matrix vs diffusive/Cattaneo/ballistic regimes
geometry: Bulk highly oriented pyrolytic / natural graphite excited by sub-nanosecond optical Transient Thermal Gratings (TTG) with spatial periods L = 5 to 15 um over T = 80 to 300 K
method: Laser-induced TTG optical heterodyne diffraction monitoring thermoelastic surface ripple u(t)*cos(qx), directly compared against parameter-free ab initio DFT + phonon BTE simulations and hydrodynamic regime maps
main_result: Directly observes oscillatory sign-reversing thermal-grating decay — unambiguous phonon second sound — in graphite at temperatures 85-125 K (nearly an order of magnitude warmer than cryogenic NaF/Bi), matching parameter-free ab initio phonon BTE predictions and mapping the diffusive-hydrodynamic-ballistic window in (T, L)
validation: Quantitative agreement between optical heterodyne TTG experimental waveforms (sign reversal at L = 7.5-10 um, T = 85-125 K) and parameter-free ab initio phonon BTE calculations
stated_limitations: Second sound in natural-isotope graphite damps out above ~125-150 K due to umklapp/isotope resistive scattering and transitions to ballistic transport at short grating periods L < 5 um
future_work: Explore isotopically pure graphite, graphene, and 2D materials where hydrodynamic phonon second sound is predicted to persist up to or near room temperature for microelectronic heat spreading

title: Nonclassical dynamical thermoelasticity
journal: International Journal of Solids and Structures
model_constitutive: Survey comparing five coupled dynamical thermoelasticity theories: Classical Biot (1956), Lord-Shulman (L-S, 1967), Green-Lindsay (G-L, 1972), Hetnarski-Ignaczak Low-Temperature Nonlinear Thermoelasticity (H-I, 1996), Green-Naghdi Type II TEWOED (G-N, 1993), and Chandrasekharaiah-Tzou Dual-Phase-Lag (C-T, 1998)
geometry: 3D isotropic/anisotropic IBVP domains and 1D transient half-space / thermal-shock benchmarks
method: Axiomatic comparison of constitutive postulates, domain-of-influence / uniqueness theorems, stress-only (Ignaczak) formulations, and wavefront jump/soliton structures
main_result: Contrasts mathematical structure, domain-of-influence bounds, and physical applicability of L-S, G-L, H-I (nonlinear cryogenic T^3 specific-heat/conductivity model yielding thermoelastic solitons), G-N Type II, and C-T phase-lag hierarchies
validation: Cross-comparison of analytical wavefront speeds, attenuation factors, and uniqueness/domain-of-influence theorems across all five nonclassical models
stated_limitations: Review/survey article; notes C-T requires Taylor-series truncations producing a sequence of approximate IBVPs whose higher-order mathematical properties remain open
future_work: Further mathematical analysis and material-specific experimental calibration of low-temperature nonlinear (H-I), TEWOED, and DPL (C-T) hyperbolic thermoelastic theories

title: A General Theory of Heat Conduction with Finite Wave Speeds
authors: Morton E. Gurtin; A. C. Pipkin
journal: Archive for Rational Mechanics and Analysis
model_constitutive: Nonlinear fading-memory rigid heat conductor depending on present temperature theta(t), summed history of temperature, and summed history of temperature gradient g_bar^t(s) = int_{t-s}^t grad(theta)(tau) dtau; linearizes to integrodifferential wave-like heat equation with kernels beta(s), alpha(s)
geometry: Rigid anisotropic/isotropic 3D heat-conducting body; 1D nonlinear acceleration waves and linearized harmonic/discontinuity waves
method: Coleman-Mizel Hilbert-space fading-memory thermodynamics deriving both entropy AND heat flux directly as Frechet derivatives of the free-energy functional, plus singular-surface wave-speed analysis
main_result: Constructs the foundational Gurtin-Pipkin memory theory of heat conduction in which heat flux is determined by the free energy functional, derives the linearized integrodifferential hyperbolic heat equation (reducing to Cattaneo's telegrapher equation for exponential alpha(s) and beta'=0), and computes finite thermal acceleration-wave speeds
validation: Rigorous Coleman-Noll/Coleman-Mizel thermodynamic consistency proofs and exact specialization to Cattaneo-Vernotte and Fourier limits
stated_limitations: Rigid heat conductor only (no mechanical deformation or thermal expansion coupling)
future_work: Extend the summed-history free-energy constitutive framework to deformable thermoelastic continua

title: Thermoelasticity without energy dissipation
authors: A. E. Green; P. M. Naghdi
model_constitutive: Nonlinear and linearized Green-Naghdi Type II thermoelasticity (TEWOED) using thermal displacement alpha (dot(alpha) = T) and beta = grad(alpha) with identically zero internal entropy production xi = 0: q = -k*grad(alpha) (so dot(q) = -k*grad(theta))
geometry: Arbitrary 3D finite/infinitesimal anisotropic and isotropic thermoelastic body Omega under mixed thermomechanical boundary conditions
method: Green-Naghdi entropy balance equality + reduced energy identity exploitation, exact energy conservation proof, and Brun-type Lagrange-identity uniqueness theorem without definiteness assumptions on elastic/conductivity tensors
main_result: Formulates nonlinear and linear Type II thermoelasticity without energy dissipation (undamped finite-speed coupled thermoelastic waves) and proves uniqueness of the mixed IBVP in bounded isotropic/anisotropic domains WITHOUT requiring positive definiteness of the elasticity or thermal-conductivity tensors (requiring only positive density and specific heat)
validation: Rigorous thermodynamic identity and Lagrange-identity uniqueness proofs; comparison against classical Type I thermoelasticity
stated_limitations: Zero internal thermal dissipation (xi = 0) implies thermal and thermoelastic waves propagate with zero attenuation (conservative limit)
future_work: Combine reversible Type II and dissipative Type I mechanisms (leading to Type III thermoelasticity)

title: A re-examination of the basic postulates of thermomechanics
authors: A. E. Green; P. M. Naghdi
journal: Proceedings of the Royal Society of London. Series A
model_constitutive: Foundational Green-Naghdi thermomechanics introducing thermal displacement scalar alpha(X, t) (with dot(alpha) = T), entropy balance as an exact equality with internal entropy generation rate xi, reduced energy identity rho*(dot(psi)+eta*dot(theta)) + p.g + rho*theta*xi = 0, and Types I, II, and III heat flow in rigid and deformable continua (including couples)
geometry: Discrete Newtonian particle systems, rigid bodies, stationary rigid 3D heat conductors, and general 3D deformable continua (with and without couple stresses)
method: Postulational re-derivation of linear/angular momentum and entropy balance laws, cyclic work/heat Second Law inequalities, invariance under superposed rigid-body motions (SRBM), and exact energy-identity constitutive reduction
main_result: Introduces the thermal displacement variable alpha and constructs three distinct thermodynamically consistent heat-conduction classes — Type I (classical Fourier), Type II (dissipationless thermal waves, xi = 0), and Type III (combined alpha-gradient and T-gradient conduction supporting damped finite-speed waves) — extending them to full thermomechanics with and without couple stresses
validation: Recovers Newtonian rigid-body dynamics, classical Fourier conduction (Type I, k >= 0), and undamped hyperbolic thermal wave equation (Type II) from a unified postulate set
stated_limitations: Foundational constitutive/postulational paper; detailed coupled deformable Type II/III initial-boundary-value and wave problems deferred to subsequent papers
future_work: Develop full nonlinear and linear thermoelasticity of Types II and III in deformable solids (carried out in Green & Naghdi 1992, 1993)

title: Thermoelasticity
authors: A. E. Green; K. A. Lindsay
model_constitutive: Nonlinear and linearized Green-Lindsay temperature-rate-dependent thermoelasticity (TRDTE) based on Green-Laws generalized thermodynamic temperature phi(theta, dot(theta)), yielding two relaxation times (alpha_0 / tau_1 in stress and entropy, alpha / tau_0 in heat equation) while retaining q_i = -k_ij theta_,j in centrosymmetric media
geometry: Arbitrary 3D homogeneous anisotropic and centrosymmetric/isotropic thermoelastic body B
method: Green-Laws generalized entropy inequality exploitation with dependence on (e_AB, theta, dot(theta), theta_,A), linearization around reference state, and energy uniqueness proof
main_result: Establishes the foundational two-relaxation-time Green-Lindsay theory of hyperbolic thermoelasticity without modifying Fourier's law in centrosymmetric bodies, derives thermodynamic inequalities (d*alpha_0 - h^2 >= 0, k_ij positive definite), and proves IBVP uniqueness
validation: Rigorous thermodynamic derivation from Green-Laws entropy inequality and reduction to classical thermoelasticity when rate parameters vanish
stated_limitations: Dependence of stress on temperature rate dot(theta) allows stress jumps ahead of strain continuity under step thermal boundary loads; restricted to homogeneous reference bodies for phi = phi(theta, dot(theta))
future_work: None explicitly stated

title: Mittag-Leffler Functions, Related Topics and Applications
authors: Rudolf Gorenflo; Anatoly A. Kilbas; Francesco Mainardi; Sergei V. Rogosin
model_constitutive: Mathematical monograph on 1-, 2-, 3- (Prabhakar), and 2n-parameter Mittag-Leffler entire functions, complete monotonicity, Laplace/Mellin/Hankel transforms, fractional relaxation/oscillation ODEs, fractional Zener/Kelvin-Voigt viscoelasticity (Ch. 7-8), anomalous diffusion/wave equations, and CTRW stochastic processes (Ch. 9)
geometry: Complex z-plane (entire-function asymptotics/Hankel contours), 1D/3D anomalous diffusion-wave domains, and rheological viscoelastic elements
method: Hankel-contour integral representations, Mellin-Barnes integrals, Laplace transform operational calculus, Bernstein complete-monotonicity characterization, and numerical computation algorithms
main_result: Provides definitive analytical theory, complete-monotonicity proofs (0 < alpha <= 1, beta >= alpha), asymptotic expansions, numerical evaluation schemes, and fractional-viscoelastic / anomalous-diffusion / wave-interpolation applications of classical and generalized Mittag-Leffler kernels
validation: Rigorous complex-analytic proofs, spectral/creep-relaxation plots for fractional Zener solids, and validated numerical evaluation algorithms across the complex plane
stated_limitations: Primarily analytical/special-function theory and linear fractional ODE/PDE applications
future_work: Open problems in multi-index/Prabhakar complete monotonicity, nonlinear fractional differential equations, and multi-scale stochastic transport

title: Fractional Calculus: Integral and Differential Equations of Fractional Order
journal: CISM Courses and Lectures No. 378 (Fractals and Fractional Calculus in Continuum Mechanics, Springer)
model_constitutive: Riemann-Liouville vs Caputo fractional integral/differential operators applied to Abel integral equations, fractional relaxation and fractional oscillation equations (0 < alpha < 1 and 1 < alpha < 2), and linear fractional viscoelasticity
geometry: Time half-line t >= 0 (initial-value problems with physically interpretable integer-order initial conditions in Caputo form)
method: Laplace-transform operational calculus, Hankel-contour spectral decomposition into completely monotonic creep/relaxation part plus decaying oscillatory residue part, and Mittag-Leffler asymptotics
main_result: Demonstrates why Caputo fractional derivatives (rather than Riemann-Liouville) naturally accommodate standard physical initial conditions in continuum mechanics, and decomposes fractional relaxation/oscillation solutions into a power-law algebraic tail plus exponentially damped oscillations for 1 < alpha < 2
validation: Exact Laplace-Hankel analytical solutions recovering exponential decay (alpha=1) and undamped harmonic oscillation (alpha=2) with explicit spectral density plots
stated_limitations: Tutorial lecture notes restricted to linear time-fractional integral/ordinary differential equations (spatial PDEs covered in companion lectures)
future_work: Wider adoption of Mittag-Leffler functions and Caputo operators across viscoelasticity, wave propagation, and anomalous diffusion

title: Stability and Second Law of Thermodynamics in dual-phase-lag heat conduction
journal: International Journal of Heat and Mass Transfer
model_constitutive: Exact time-retarded Tzou Dual-Phase-Lag (DPL) rigid heat conduction q(x, t + tau_q) = -K*grad(T)(x, t + tau_T) AND 2nd-order-tau_q / 2nd-order-tau_T Taylor-approximated Jeffreys/DPL PDE, tested against cyclic Clausius-Duhem / Second Law dissipation on sinusoidal histories
geometry: Bounded smooth 3D rigid heat-conducting domain Omega with homogeneous Dirichlet/Neumann thermal boundary conditions
method: Fourier/Laplace half-range cosine-transform positivity test of cyclic Second-Law dissipation combined with exponential/delay-differential stability root analysis
main_result: Proves that exact time-delayed DPL heat conduction satisfies cyclic Second-Law positivity and delay-differential stability ONLY in the degenerate synchronous case tau_q = tau_T (classical Fourier!), and shows that in 2nd-order Taylor DPL, thermodynamic cyclic dissipation inequalities are strictly WEAKER than the Routh-Hurwitz asymptotic stability region (tau_T/tau_q in (sqrt(2)-1, sqrt(2)+1) fails stability despite satisfying cyclic Second Law)
validation: Explicit analytical counterexamples (harmonics violating cosine-transform positivity for tau_q != tau_T and unstable modes inside thermodynamically admissible parameter regions)
stated_limitations: Rigid heat conductor only; highlights fundamental incompatibility between naive time-shift phase-lag laws, cyclic Second Law, and PDE well-posedness/stability
future_work: Questions whether cyclic Second-Law formulations must be supplemented by a priori state-space admissibility or replaced by genuine fading-memory / Guyer-Krumhansl / MGT models

title: Theory of fractional order in generalized thermoelectric MHD
model_constitutive: 1D generalized magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) thermoelectric fluid/medium combining Jumarie modified Riemann-Liouville fractional Taylor-expanded Cattaneo heat flux (1 + (tau_0^alpha / alpha!) d^alpha/dt^alpha) q = -kappa I^(gamma-1) grad(T) with Peltier/Seebeck thermoelectric coupling and Lorentz drag
geometry: Semi-infinite 1D electrically and thermally conducting fluid half-space y >= 0 bounded by a suddenly heated moving/stationary plane under transverse magnetic field B_0
method: Laplace-transform 4x4 state-space matrix exponential formulation inverted numerically via Honig-Hirdes Fourier-series Laplace inversion
main_result: Derives a two-parameter (alpha, gamma) time-fractional thermoelectric MHD model incorporating the thermoelectric figure-of-merit Z*T_0 and computes transient temperature, velocity, induced current, and heat-flux profiles across fractional orders
validation: Limiting-case comparisons at alpha = 1, gamma = 1 against standard Cattaneo-Lord-Shulman MHD heat-transfer profiles
stated_limitations: Relies on Jumarie's fractional Taylor series (later criticized in fractional-calculus literature regarding chain/Leibniz rules); 1D half-space numerical Laplace inversion without experimental validation
future_work: Classify thermoelectric materials experimentally via effective fractional parameters (alpha, gamma) to optimize ZT performance

title: On Nonlocal Elasticity
authors: A. Cemal Eringen; D. G. B. Edelen
model_constitutive: Nonlinear finite-strain nonlocal thermoelasticity formulated via global mass/momentum/moment-of-momentum/energy/entropy balance laws localized with zero-mean nonlocal localization residuals (rho_hat, f_hat_k, l_hat_k, e_hat, eta_hat)
geometry: Arbitrary 3D finite-strain deformable nonlocal continuum B; static homogeneous extensions and 1D plane wave example
method: Comparison of localized Clausius-Duhem inequality vs global Gibbsian variational thermodynamics on Banach spaces of whole-body deformation/temperature fields using Frechet derivatives and objectivity invariance
main_result: Establishes the nonlinear Eringen-Edelen framework of nonlocal elasticity with localization residuals, derives constitutive relations for stress, heat flux, entropy, and nonlocal body-force/energy residuals under both localized Clausius-Duhem and global Gibbsian approaches, and linearizes to integral nonlocal elasticity
validation: Consistency checks between Gibbsian and Clausius-Duhem reductions and exact recovery of classical nonlinear hyperelasticity when nonlocal Frechet kernels vanish
stated_limitations: Nonlocal localization residuals remain partly undetermined in full generality unless restricted by symmetry/homogeneity; heat flux remains instantaneous (no thermal memory/relaxation)
future_work: Specialize to linear isotropic nonlocal elasticity and calibrate nonlocal kernels against lattice dispersion (carried out in Eringen 1972, Int. J. Engng Sci. 10, 425)

title: Linear Theory of Micropolar Elasticity
model_constitutive: Linear isotropic micropolar (Cosserat) elasticity with independent displacement vector u_k and microrotation vector phi_k, micro-inertia i_km, asymmetric force stress t_kl, and couple stress m_kl governed by 6 isotropic elastic moduli (lambda, mu, kappa, alpha, beta, gamma)
geometry: Arbitrary 3D bounded regular micropolar body V with boundary S under mixed displacement/microrotation and traction/couple-traction boundary conditions
method: Reduction from general micromorphic elasticity, thermodynamic/strain-energy positive-definiteness inequalities on the 6 moduli, and energy/divergence-theorem uniqueness proofs
main_result: Formulates linear micropolar elasticity (6 moduli, determinate asymmetric stress tensor), proves couple-stress elasticity emerges as the constrained limit phi_k = (1/2) curl(u)_k, derives exact thermodynamic positivity bounds on (lambda, mu, kappa, alpha, beta, gamma), and proves dynamic and static uniqueness theorems
validation: Rigorous strain-energy positivity and dynamic/static uniqueness theorems plus exact reduction to constrained couple-stress and classical Navier-Cauchy elasticity
stated_limitations: Isothermal linear theory (energy/entropy stated in general balance laws, then specialized to isothermal micropolar elasticity)
future_work: Apply linear micropolar field equations to granular, fibrous, and dumbbell-molecule boundary-value and wave problems
